record.original_question: How can nature-inspired optimization algorithms that work well on small-scale problem instances be scaled up so that they solve truly large-scale real-world problems efficiently?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. How to best scale up the algorithms that work well for small-scale problems to solve truly large-scale, real-world problems efficiently?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithms (for example, evolutionary algorithms, particle swarm optimization, ant colony optimization, differential evolution, firefly algorithm, cuckoo search, and similar population-based stochastic search methods) designed to approximately solve optimization problems of the form

  minimize f(x)  subject to  x ∈ Ω ⊆ R^n,

where f : Ω → R may be nonlinear, nonconvex, multimodal, noisy, or only available as a black-box oracle, and Ω may be defined by complicated (possibly nonlinear or combinatorial) constraints.

It is empirically established that many such algorithms perform well on small-scale instances (with n at most a few tens of variables and modest numbers of constraints). Develop a systematic methodology — including algorithmic modifications, theoretical analysis of convergence and complexity, and guidelines for parameter tuning, decomposition, parallelization, dimensionality reduction, surrogate modelling, and constraint handling — that allows such algorithms to be scaled up so that they solve truly large-scale real-world optimization problems (with n on the order of 10^4 to 10^6 or more variables, and large numbers of constraints) efficiently, in the sense of producing high-quality solutions within practically acceptable computational budgets. Specifically: identify general principles that govern when and how a small-scale nature-inspired algorithm can be extended to the large-scale regime while preserving solution quality, and provide quantitative performance guarantees as functions of problem dimension, structure, and computational resources.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of efficiently scaling nature-inspired (metaheuristic) optimization algorithms to truly large-scale, real-world instances is widely treated as an open research challenge in the evolutionary and swarm computation literature. Active research areas include cooperative coevolution, large-scale global optimization (LSGO) benchmarks, surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms, and decomposition-based methods, but no general solution providing universal scalability with performance guarantees is known.

status_evidence.title: Large-scale global optimization: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys methods for large-scale global optimization and notes that scaling metaheuristics to high-dimensional real-world problems remains a major open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Scaling nature-inspired algorithms to large-scale problems is recognized as an active and open research area.
